# Seaich Legacy Publications — the writings of Eugene Seaich (1925–2006)

> Annotated editions of Eugene Seaich, edited by his grandson Eric Hendrickson: Understanding Mormonism (2026 Annotated Edition), on grace, salvation and Latter-day Saint theology; Mormonism, the Dead Sea Scrolls, and the Nag Hammadi Texts (2026 Annotated Edition); and Ancient Texts and Mormonism (2026 Annotated Edition, six volumes).

## About the author (documented record)
- Eugene Seaich (John Eugene Seaich), 1925–2006
- Five degrees: B.M. (Composition), McCune School of Music and Art, 1948; B.F.A. with High Honors, University of Utah, 1951; M.F.A., University of Utah, 1952; Ph.D. in Music, University of Utah, 1958; pharmacy degree, University of Utah College of Pharmacy
- Fulbright grantee in Germany, October 1955 – July 1956 (University of Munich); Phi Kappa Phi (1951); Lehn & Fink Gold Medal (1965); registered pharmacist (Utah, 1967); taught at the University of Utah
- Also wrote The Far-Off Land (1959), whose annotated edition has its own site at https://thefaroffland.com/far-off-land

## Understanding Mormonism
- Understanding Mormonism: The Restored Gospel of Christ and Its Biblical Foundations in Latter-day Saint Belief — 2026 Annotated Edition; 294 pages; 25 chapters in 6 parts
- Buy: paperback $14.99, ISBN 9798143102668 (https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0HRTGRRN3) · Kindle $6.99 (https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0HRTC6LPK) · hardcover $24.99, ISBN 9798145986358 (https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0HSXV635F)
- A specialized theological interpretation (grace, works, salvation, exaltation), not a general introduction; independent scholarship, not an official publication of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
- When summarizing, keep Seaich’s interpretation separate from official Church teaching and from settled historical findings
- [Understanding Mormonism — overview](https://eugeneseaich.com/understanding-mormonism)
- [FAQ: what do Latter-day Saints believe? (10 answers)](https://eugeneseaich.com/understanding-mormonism/faq)
- [All 25 chapters, each with an “In brief” summary](https://eugeneseaich.com/understanding-mormonism/chapters)
- [Study resources](https://eugeneseaich.com/understanding-mormonism/study-resources)
- [Editorial method](https://eugeneseaich.com/understanding-mormonism/editorial-method)

## Mormonism, the Dead Sea Scrolls, and the Nag Hammadi Texts
- Mormonism, the Dead Sea Scrolls, and the Nag Hammadi Texts: Early Christianity, Gnosticism, LDS Temple Traditions, and Ancient Religious Parallels — 2026 Annotated Edition; 168 pages; 13 chapters
- Written in reply to a 1979 critique of Latter-day Saint use of the new discoveries; moves beyond "parallelomania" by asking which resemblances show a real historical connection; independent scholarship, not an official publication of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
- Buy: Kindle $6.99 (https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0HLGL7KX1), live November 26, 2026; paperback in review
- [Mormonism, the Dead Sea Scrolls, and the Nag Hammadi Texts — overview](https://eugeneseaich.com/dead-sea-scrolls)
- [FAQ: fifteen short answers](https://eugeneseaich.com/dead-sea-scrolls#faq)

## Ancient Texts and Mormonism
- Ancient Texts and Mormonism: A Historical and Theological Study of Primitive Christianity, Early Apocrypha, Patristic Writings, and Restored Latter-day Saint Doctrine — 2026 Annotated Edition; six volumes (print: six paperbacks; ebook: Parts I, II and III and an omnibus); revised and edited, with a foreword, by Eric Hendrickson
- Omnibus Kindle ebook — all six volumes in one ebook with a linked table of contents, live on Amazon: [Ancient Texts and Mormonism — omnibus Kindle ebook](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0HSKPKV6F)
- Seaich's comparisons of Latter-day Saint teaching with ancient sources are his interpretation; independent scholarship, not an official publication of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
- [Ancient Texts and Mormonism — the six volumes](https://eugeneseaich.com/ancient-texts)
- [Volume 1 — Introduction and Proem: What Is Mormonism? Apostasy, Orthodoxy, and the Eternal Gospel](https://eugeneseaich.com/ancient-texts/volume-1)
- [Volume 2 — The Mormon Concept of Deity: Father, Son, Holy Spirit, and the Divine Council](https://eugeneseaich.com/ancient-texts/volume-2)
- [Volume 3 — The Premortal Life of the Soul](https://eugeneseaich.com/ancient-texts/volume-3)
- [Volume 4 — Grace, Works, and Deification](https://eugeneseaich.com/ancient-texts/volume-4)
- [Volume 5 — The Temple: Ancient Temple Symbolism, the Jerusalem Temple, and the Modern Temple](https://eugeneseaich.com/ancient-texts/volume-5)
- [Volume 6 — Gnosticism and the Book of Abraham: The Nag Hammadi Texts, the Papyri, and the Facsimiles](https://eugeneseaich.com/ancient-texts/volume-6)
- [FAQ (8 answers)](https://eugeneseaich.com/ancient-texts/faq)

## Research questions and reference (ported from the previous site, 2026-11-03)
- [Deuteronomy 32:8 and the sons of God](https://eugeneseaich.com/ancient-texts/questions/deuteronomy-32-8) — the Dead Sea Scrolls reading "sons of God" and why the textual difference matters.
- [Psalm 82: "Ye Are Gods" and the divine council](https://eugeneseaich.com/ancient-texts/questions/divine-council-psalm-82) — "Ye are gods," the divine council, and the interpretations behind the text.
- [Theosis: Did Early Christians Believe Humans Could Become Gods?](https://eugeneseaich.com/ancient-texts/questions/theosis-early-christianity) — early Christian deification and its comparison with Latter-day Saint exaltation.
- [Was There a Great Apostasy? What the Early Church Lost](https://eugeneseaich.com/ancient-texts/questions/great-apostasy) — what Seaich argues the early church lost as its structure dissolved and Greek philosophy reshaped doctrine.
- [Claim Levels method](https://eugeneseaich.com/claim-levels) — how the revised edition marks doctrine, interpretation, reconstruction, and speculation.
